probe_A.question: Does K44's directional-sender failure originate from unsupervised boundary queries, invalid directional flux, or another identifiable operator limitation?
probe_A.state: first-event (sun only, L = 0; worklog 45 verified field) for energy accounting; converged production state for directional distributions
probe_A.groups: classes Yellow (mat 0) and opaque (mats 1, 3, 5, 6, 7) x observed / never observed (training-probe pixels mapped to the port, stagea/prep2_train px_dom == 0) x lit / shadow (Esun > 0 in the view); up to 1500 ports per cell per view, seed 4801

queries.camera: up to 8 training camera directions of the port (px_cam)
queries.C_requested: up to 16 directions -d of rel_T0 gathers that hit the port

measures: nonlocal (glob + band + mid) and local (production 'E') luminance per query
anisotropy AI = max / min over the 19 bin centres (nonlocal)
F = cosine-weighted hemispherical mean / normal value
dev(dir) = |log(L(dir) / L_cosmean)| for supervised (within 10 deg of a training camera direction of that port) vs unsupervised (> 20 deg from all) directions at observed ports

domain energy accounting on the first-event field: Lego outgoing flux (hemispherical, 64 cosine directions, all K parts) / sun power absorbed by Lego ports; also the production normal-direction flux; 200k-port random subsample
probe_A.physical_reference: worklog 47 SSS: Yellow nonlocal exit radiance at top / +y45 / -y45 cameras (shadow bands, field A, both replicates) -> measured anisotropy of Cycles' Yellow nonlocal exit

criteria.output_invalid: Yellow nonlocal median AI > 1.5 (both views) OR first-event Lego hemispherical outgoing / absorbed flux > 1
criteria.port_supervision_association: median AI (Yellow never observed) >= 1.5 x median AI (Yellow observed), both views
criteria.direction_supervision_association: at observed Yellow ports, median dev(unsupervised) >= 1.5 x median dev(supervised), both views
criteria.classification: supervision hypothesis supported if output_invalid and both associations hold; representation-or-other if output_invalid and neither association holds; mixed otherwise

probe_B.question: Do K44's spatial support and low-rank structures impose a measurable approximation limit on the Yellow nonlocal (Burley) response?
probe_B.oracle: worklog 45 Burley operator (A1a-fitted d_R/G/B = 6.09 / 1.20 / 0.39 cm, truncation 16 d, r >= 2 mm), object-scoped sources (all Lego ports), self port excluded (owned by K_loc); 2000 Yellow receiver ports (seed 4802) x 852,358 fine source ports; Hilbert-Schmidt weighting sqrt(A_x) k(x, s) sqrt(A_s)

conditions.B1_S5: exact kernel within the band support (r < 5 cm), 0 beyond (Frobenius-optimal support-limited operator)
conditions.B1_S30: exact within the mid support (r < 30 cm), 0 beyond
conditions.B1_Q: K44's actual support structure with ideal weights: band = 96 representative 1.5 cm aggregates (anchors nbr / nbrA) x cell-average kernel over r < 5 cm, applied to the area-mean field; mid = 128 representative 8 cm cells (mid / midA) x cell-average kernel over r >= 5 cm; i.e. support + aggregation + representative quadrature with a perfectly learned weight
conditions.B1_Q_G64: B1_Q + the best rank-64 approximation of the residual (Eckart-Young on the 2000 receivers: an optimistic bound for the domain-wide rank-64 global)
conditions.B1_S30_G64: B1_S30 + best rank-64 of the tail
conditions.B2_r: best rank-r of the full operator, r in {8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256}
conditions.B3: upper bound = the reference (0 error) - not needed as a separate run

probe_B.fields: 16 held-out T0 view sun fields E = E_SUN max(0, n.l) frac (eval_vis_k44), response y = sum_s k A_s E_s
measures: field-response relative L2 per channel: all / lit / shadow receivers
by distance of the receiver to the nearest lit port: 0-1, 1-3, 3-10, 10-30, > 30 cm
pairs excluded by support (HS mass beyond 5 / 30 cm)
probe_B.k44_comparison: K44 first-event nonlocal (glob + band + mid at the port normal) vs the oracle response scaled by worklog 45's per-channel object-scope factors s_c, on shadow receivers (red), same receivers / views

criteria.rank_binding: B1_Q_G64 shadow error (R) >= 0.10 (the global rank-64 cannot recover what support / aggregation lose)
criteria.fitting_accounts: K44 shadow error (R) >= 2 x B1_Q_G64 shadow error (R)

probe_C.question: Why do worklog 46's directional reads improve static glossy fidelity while degrading edit tracking in some views?
probe_C.scene: worklog 46 MS (Lego + box + analytic GGX plane, alpha 0.04), geometry / IS rays / references unchanged; views 0, 1, 2 (view 2 = problematic, 0 / 1 controls), T0 and T1

conditions.C0: R6a (iso senders, plane IS) - stored worklog-46 predictions; baseline check = recomputed
conditions.C1: R6br (19-bin basis reads into the plane + IS) - stored worklog-46 predictions
conditions.C2: exact per-ray nonlocal sender queries for every read into the plane (gathers and IS pixel rays), everything else as C1 (production K solve semantics, loc 'E', sun lobe)
conditions.C2b: diagnostic: basis reads in C2's converged state (separates read approximation from solve-state difference)

measures: per-ray basis / exact sender ratio by hit class (Yellow / opaque / glass / box)
edit corr / slope / explained / sign agreement on plane pixels in both states
changed-pixel error (|dr| > 3 sigma, sigma = view-0 replicate)
timing: solve, basis build, exact reads, IS pixel reads; peak memory

kf_secondary.data: worklog 46 emit46 oracle (kappa 0 / 2 / 8, views 6 / 15, replicate kappa 8 view 6), same 20,000 non-Yellow pixels (seed 4602)

arms.K1: worklog 46 R2 (receiver-port gathers, field at the hit port origin, port normal)
arms.K2: same rays, field and true triangle normal at the exact hit point (removes sender port position / aggregation)
arms.K3: 128 cosine rays from the pixel's own position and normal, exact hit field (removes receiver aggregation)
arms.K4: as K3 with 2048 rays (limited sampling control: quadrature)

kf_secondary.rules: inside faces (-2) and misses carry 0 in every arm; clean subset = pixels with near-hit fraction <= 0.05 and inside fraction <= 0.10 reported beside 'all'
